title: consistent-chunk-anchoring-and-json-seam-repair-for-sse
author: Aisha Gomez
description: Context: Customers reported intermittent malformed JSON being emitted from the SSE endpoint when streams are under bursty load and when tool/function call handoffs occur. Root causes identified: (1) jitter in chunk boundary alignment that produced half-escaped UTF-8 sequences across SSE events, (2) race between the streaming flusher and the fncall sentinel insertion which could reorder sentinel tokens relative to trailing delimiters, and (3) OpenAI-compat adapter rebuffering that coalesced unrelated events into a single SSE data frame. Motivation: fix hard-to-reproduce partial-JSON cases without regressing latency or throughput. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a lightweight chunk anchoring metadata byte (anchor flag) in the stream encoder so that receivers can detect when a chunk boundary is semantically safe to reemit a delimiter; this avoids the heuristics that previously caused delimiter duplication or loss. 2) Add a JSON seam repair step in the SSE reassembler that detects incomplete UTF-8/JSON spans at the chunk edge and emits a deterministic continuation marker ("__REDWOOD_JSON_SEAM__") only when necessary; the OpenAI compatibility layer rewrites these markers to a safe no-op event for downstream SDKs. 3) Tighten the fncall handshake: we now reserve a one-byte fence and apply ordered publish semantics so function-call sentinel insertion wins the race against the flusher without introducing extra buffering. 4) Reduce coalescing in the OpenAI adapter: switch from block-coalesce to affinity-based coalesce so events from different logical streams are not merged in the same SSE data block. 5) Add comprehensive unit + fuzz tests that simulate chunk splits at UTF-8 and JSON token boundaries and end-to-end integration tests using the openai-compat shim. Migration & compatibility: default behavior is backward-compatible; the chunk anchoring flag is opt-in for private deployments via config sse.chunk_anchor=true and is enabled for Hosted rollout after a staged canary. OpenAI-compat consumers see no breaking behavior: the repair marker is transformed to an internal no-op event. Checklist: - [x] Implement chunk anchor encoding/decoding - [x] Implement JSON seam repair and seam-to-noop mapping in openai-compat - [x] Tighten fncall handshake and add ordered publish path - [x] Swap coalescing strategy in openai adapter - [x] Add unit/fuzz/integration tests - [x] Update streaming docs and SDK guidance - [x] Run canary and smoke test on dedicated cluster Tests & validation: unit tests cover 92% of the new streaming module, fuzz tests run 50k iterations covering splits on multi-byte UTF-8 and nested JSON tokens, integration test uses local harness to validate toolcall ordering under 1000 concurrent streams. Linked issues: SUP-1142 (customer incident), ENG-8423 (streaming robustness epic).

fix: json seam detection and continuation marker
chore: upgrade openai-compat shim to map seam marker to noop event
fix: ordered fncall publish path and fence reservation
perf: switch openai adapter to affinity coalesce
test: add fuzz harness for chunk-split edgecases
docs: streaming behavior and migration notes
review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain why we need a marker instead of attempting to reassemble at the consumer? Author: The marker is a cheap sentinel that avoids repeated expensive reassembly attempts under backpressure and is only emitted when a true seam is detected.

Marceline Duarte: The fence byte sounds risky for portability across proxies. Author: We keep it as an internal in-band flag, encoded as a low-entropy prefix in the chunk header; adapters that can't parse it will ignore and fall back to heuristics (backwards-compatible).
Priya Nair: Please add an observability metric for seam events. Author: Added metric streaming.seam_repaired_count and dashboard tile in streaming ops bar. Reviewers: LGTM after tests pass.
release_notes: Fixes a rare class of malformed partial-JSON responses emitted by the SSE streaming endpoint under bursty load and function-call handoffs. Adds chunk anchoring to improve delimiter stability and a deterministic seam repair path. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via sse.chunk_anchor config for private deployments. Recommended for all Hosted users once canary completes.
notes: Rollout plan: enable in a 5% hosted canary for 48 hours, monitor streaming.seam_repaired_count and error.rate, then 25% for 24h, then full rollout. For Dedicated/Private, enable via config or coordinate upgrade with infra team. Observability: new metrics and a Grafana dashboard tile were added (streaming.seam_repaired_count, streaming.chunk_anchor_accepted).
